lines.text: Moses tells Israel to appoint judges in every town, who must not accept bribes, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise.
Israel must not set up a wooden Asherah pole beside the LORD's altar or sacrifice a flawed ox or sheep.
After investigating a report, Israel may stone a person for worshiping other gods only on the testimony of twelve witnesses.
Cases too difficult for the town go to the Levitical scribes at the place the LORD will choose, and their verdict must be followed.
The king the LORD chooses must come from among Israel's brothers, avoid many horses and wives, and read his scroll all his life.
